Anaharath
an-uh-HAY-rath
proper noun
A town in the inheritance of the tribe of Issachar, named in the roll of its cities; the name is taken to mean “a gorge” or “a narrow pass.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Anaharath was a town in the inheritance of Issachar, named with its neighbors: “And Hapharaim, and Shion, and Anaharath” (Jos 19:19). It is named nowhere else, a town likely set at or named for a narrow gorge or defile in the hills of Issachar. If the name indeed signify a narrow pass, it may serve the reader as a meditation on one of the Lord’s most solemn sayings, that the way of life is a narrow way. “Enter ye in at the strait gate…because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it” (Mat 7:13-14). The road to destruction is broad, and the crowd streams down it; but the way to life is a narrow pass, hemmed in on either hand by the commandments of God, and travelled by few. This narrowness is not the meanness of a grudging religion but the safety of a guarded road: the walls that hem the way are the walls that keep the traveller from the precipice. A town named for a narrow pass reminds the believer to seek the strait gate, to walk the fenced and narrow road of obedience, and not to be carried along with the multitude on the broad way. Few find it; but he that endureth to the end, walking the narrow pass with Christ who is the way, shall come at last to the city of life.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Issachar whose name means “a narrow pass”; a meditation on the strait gate and narrow way that leadeth unto life.

expand to see more

ANAHARATH, a town in the inheritance of Issachar.

It is named with its neighbors in the roll of Issachar’s cities (Jos 19:19).

The name is taken to mean a gorge, or a narrow pass.

It may serve as a meditation on the narrow way that leadeth unto life.

The road to destruction is broad, but the way to life is narrow.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 19:19 — "And Hapharaim, and Shion, and Anaharath,"

Mat 7:13 — "Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat :"

Mat 7:14 — "Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it."

Luk 13:24 — "Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A town of Scripture; it recovers the Lord’s teaching that the way to life is a narrow, guarded road, travelled by few.

expand to see more

Anaharath faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its name may carry answers the broad-way religion of the age, which reckons all roads to lead to God and scorns the strait gate as narrow-minded, forgetting the Lord’s own warning that few find the way of life.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the narrow way. If Anaharath be indeed a narrow pass, it pictures the road to life, hemmed by God’s commandments and walked by few. The narrowness is not meanness but safety, the walls that keep the traveller from the precipice; the believer seeks the strait gate and walks the fenced road with Christ, who is the way.

"Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life."
